account: vivo reports that it released vivo Sight, a visual assistance product, in 2023. It reports that it listed an upgraded version for vivo phone users in May 2024. In the CCL24-Eval shared task of July 2024, organizers from Beijing Union University and Xiamen University had deaf sign language users and certified translators rate the four sign language avatar systems that passed screening. They ranked vivo's system first with 3.513 of 5, against 2.119 for the baseline. The shared task measured the quality of avatar output on four test sentences. In its project account for the International Telecommunication Union, current as of June 2025, vivo describes on-device speech, vision and sign language features that work offline. vivo reports direct accessibility benefits for users. No source measures everyday use or the wider social effects.

Organizers from Beijing Union University, Xiamen University and Tsinghua University, funded by national science and language grants, ran a shared task in which deaf sign language users and certified sign language translators rated the four of ten submitted systems that passed preliminary screening. They have no stake in vivo. Their test measures output quality on four test sentences and has no measure of everyday use.
